A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SIGS research work, with the same title and authors. Their main texts, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial revision.

before.justification: V1 reports original SIGS solution-recovery, error, sensitivity, and runtime results in Section 3 and Appendix E. Some comparison values are explicitly borrowed from prior work, but SIGS outcomes are original.

after.justification: V2 reports original PDE evaluations, symbolic approximations, runtime comparisons, component ablations, and numerical-reference validation in Section 3 and Appendix C.

M1.justification: V1 uses a GVAE with CMA-ES latent search and subsequent self-composition. V2 introduces explicit hierarchical Ansatz-and-atom assembly, convex-enclosure, persistent-homology and decoder-smoothness regularizers, and iterative clustering followed by separate gradient-based coefficient refinement. These substantially change the training objective and solution procedure.

E1.justification: V2 removes the evaluated Tsoulos suite, including ODEs and coupled systems, and the shallow-water and 16-mode wave evaluations. It introduces literature PDE benchmarks, including linear advection, and localized Gaussian-forced Poisson problems without known analytical solutions. Burgers, diffusion, and wave coverage remains, with revised settings.

E2.justification: The GP, ACP, ABCP, and Mathematica comparisons in v1 disappear. V2 evaluates HD-TLGP under two protocols, SSDE, and FEniCS, while retaining PINNs and FBPINNs in the known-solution comparison. SSDE was discussed in v1's literature review but was not an evaluated comparator there.

E3.justification: Reported GVAE training changes include a 90/10 training/validation split becoming 70/20/10, sequence length 160 becoming 72, and batch size 20 becoming 64. Burgers evaluation extends from t=1 to t=2 and uses a denser grid; diffusion parameters also change. V2 introduces baseline budgets, time-to-tolerance reporting, and numerical-reference protocols, although some mesh and protocol descriptions conflict internally.

E4.justification: V1's boundary-weight sensitivity study, initialization trajectory analysis, and self-composition demonstration are removed. V2 adds atoms-versus-primitives and TGVAE-versus-GVAE sampling ablations, plus finite-element mesh-convergence, energy-balance, and residual checks. These investigate substantially different mechanisms and validation questions.

E5.justification: V2 introduces mean-plus/minus reporting across ten disjoint latent-sample sets for the GVAE/TGVAE ablation and discloses split seed 42. V1's reported 30-run average concerns borrowed ABCP results. V2 does not clearly identify the ablation's spread as a standard deviation or confidence interval, or establish repeated full PDE experiments.

E6.justification: V1's Tsoulos iteration results and shallow-water/16-mode-wave results disappear. V2 adds exact-recovery results on three literature benchmarks, Poisson-Gauss errors reported as 2.66%, 1.54%, and 1.05%, new comparator outcomes, runtimes, and ablation findings. Results for retained PDE families are replaced under revised methods or settings, so they do not establish same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: V1's Stone-Weierstrass density argument and derivations supporting Properties 2.1–2.4 are removed. V2 formalizes Ansatz-restricted languages and assembly, introduces geometric-regularization definitions, and develops spectral/eigenfunction constructions in Appendix A. The mathematical development changes substantially rather than merely moving or changing notation.

C1.justification: V1 foregrounds grammar-derived properties, one-solver-solves-all behavior, and performance across ODEs, PDEs, and systems. V2 makes hierarchical Ansatz-and-atom composition and TGVAE explicit central contributions, and adds claims about symbolic approximation of PDEs without known closed-form solutions. The general neuro-symbolic solution-discovery claim remains.

C2.justification: The explanation of success shifts from initialization, grammar closure, and implicit boundary satisfaction to structured atoms, latent geometry, and global/local optimization. V2 attributes symbolic-baseline failures to combinatorial search and sparse rewards, and explicitly identifies expert-chosen Ansätze as an applicability limitation. V1's numerical-constant precision limitation is no longer presented as a principal limitation.

D1.justification: V2 substantially expands reproducibility information through architecture and environment tables, atom-validation rules, search pseudocode, float64 JAX coefficient refinement, baseline hyperparameters, and finite-element procedures. V1 already supplied GVAE training details, but much of this documentation is new. V1's promised code/model/expression-library release link is omitted; this does not establish that resources were withdrawn.

R1.justification: V2 explicitly positions forward solution discovery against inverse equation discovery and centers its comparison on SSDE and newly cited HD-TLGP. It adds symbolic-regression and topology literature, including Cao et al., Yu et al., and Edelsbrunner and Harer, while removing much of v1's broader classical and neural-solver review. This substantially revises research positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, methods, and discussion are extensively rewritten, with a new contribution list and an Ansatz/TGVAE-centered narrative replacing the solver-taxonomy and four-properties organization. Appendices A–E are reorganized into A–C with a contents list. These are substantial language and structural changes beyond added scientific content.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redesigned to depict the revised search procedure. V1's ODE, shallow-water, initialization, and 16-mode-wave displays are removed; v2 adds baseline-comparison and Poisson-reference/error figures. Numerous architecture, protocol, expression, and validation tables and four algorithm boxes substantially change the visual presentation and layout.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens documentation and addresses gaps in v1 with recent symbolic comparators, tests without known analytical solutions, and component ablations. However, its near-exact Burgers recovery conflicts with the opposite shock signs in Tables 15 and 18, while Poisson reference settings differ between Appendix C.4 and Figures 7–9. The PDFs do not resolve whether these are presentation errors or evaluation problems. Consequently, the reliability of important added evidence, and the net overall quality gain, remains uncertain.
